items.title: Lawrence Duhé Interview, 1960
items.q: Mr. Dewey, what did you think about Armstrong? I mean, as much as you know about him, what do you think about him? Greatest. One in the world greatest.

ctx.x: Mr. Dewey, would you tell us some of the fine players that played with you or that you knew while you were in Chicago?

Well, I left New Orleans with Sugar Johnny, and he got in bad health, and I switched to Mud Carry. After Mud Carry, the climate was too cold. He dropped me in Chicago, came back to New Orleans and sent King Oliver with me. So King Oliver stuck with me a while later, then he sent Armstrong later. Mr. Dewey, what did you think about Armstrong? I mean, as much as you know about him, what do you think about him? Greatest. One in the world greatest. Do you like his style of playing? Oh, yes. I really do. Did he play…
Mr. Dewey, a while ago, we did not ask you any questions at all about your family background, but would you tell me, were your parents and were all the people in your family Catholic?
